query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Machine learning potentials can accurately and efficiently determine the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys across the family.
generation.intervention: Training machine learning potentials using ab initio calculations or molecular dynamics simulations
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic arrangements and bonding in high-entropy alloys
generation.mechanism: Machine learning potentials learn the complex relationships between atomic arrangements and thermodynamic properties, enabling accurate predictions
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean absolute error (MAE) in predicted melting temperatures less than 50 K, and MAE in predicted enthalpy and entropy of fusion less than 10% relative to experimental values
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of machine learning potentials for high-entropy alloys with more than 6 principal elements, and uncertainty in the transferability of the potentials to different alloy compositions

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of machine learning potential predictions with experimental values for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MAE in predicted melting temperatures exceeds 100 K, or the MAE in predicted enthalpy and entropy of fusion exceeds 20% relative to experimental values, the hypothesis is falsified
